output: {"candidate_claims":[{"claim":"When a write times out or returns a server error, the action may already have taken effect, and blind retries cause duplicate side effects while giving up skips required work.","evidence_refs":[{"page":1,"quote":"When a tool-using agent’s write times out or returns a server error, the action may already have taken effect. Retrying blindly duplicates it—a second charge, a second announcement, a second deployment—while giving up skips required work."}],"importance":"load_bearing"},{"claim":"Frontier models instructed to act exactly once almost never duplicate a write whose acknowledgement was lost, whereas weaker models often do.","evidence_refs":[{"page":1,"quote":"When an immediate read-back can reveal what happened, the model decides: frontier models instructed to act exactly once almost never duplicate a write whose acknowledgement was lost (0.5%), weaker models often do, and the model explains 53% of the explained variance."}],"importance":"load_bearing"},{"claim":"When an immediate read-back cannot reveal what happened (such as a request still in flight or redelivered), frontier models duplicate frequently and the contract explains 81% of the variance.","evidence_refs":[{"page":1,"quote":"When it cannot—the request is still in flight, or the transport delivered it twice—the same frontier models duplicate in 56% and 74% of episodes, and the contract explains 81%."}],"importance":"load_bearing"},{"claim":"No verification-only policy is exactly-once under late commits without a bound on in-flight time, and offering idempotency keys lowers the duplicate rate because agents use keys when they exist.","evidence_refs":[{"page":1,"quote":"We prove that no verification-only policy is exactly-once under late commits without a bound on in-flight time. Waiting works when such a bound is short and known, but with heavy-tailed in-flight delays even an hour of waiting per episode falls short of offering an idempotency key on every write, which lowers the duplicate rate from 28% to 4% because agents use keys when they exist."}],"importance":"load_bearing"},{"claim":"Agent harnesses matter little for exactly-once execution; client-side middleware has a ceiling, and agents reported success in 90% of duplicate-producing episodes.","evidence_refs":[{"page":1,"quote":"The harness barely matters, a guard that attaches keys transfers across harnesses unchanged, and agents reported success in 90% of the episodes in which they had duplicated an effect."}],"importance":"supporting"}],"key_claims":["Where exactly-once behaviour should be enforced depends on the fault (model vs tool contract).","Frontier models verify before retrying on resolvable faults, whereas unresolvable faults like late commits and redelivery require contract-level support such as idempotency keys.","Waiting is not a substitute for idempotency keys, especially under heavy-tailed in-flight delays.","Production harnesses behave similarly to minimal scaffolds under identical faults."],"limitations":["Simulated services and synthetic task templates were used instead of live production environments.","All models were accessed through a single gateway which fixes some provider default settings.","The heavy-tailed in-flight delay distribution is a modeling choice and specific numerical success rates depend on its shape."],"load_bearing_pages":[1,2,4,5,6,8,10,12],"requested_pages":[],"stop_reason":"All necessary pages for analyzing the requested agenda have been successfully processed."}
